1  JUDGMENT

This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 10.08.2021 at about 7.30 p.m. when the petitioner proceeding as a pillion rider in Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-EA-9620 on Doddabukkasagara road, after finishing his duty while returning back to his native place along with rider Rudresh B.R., when they reached near Parvathamma Farm, Kadur Taluk, at that time, the said Motor cycle rider rode his vehicle with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden one cow came in front of their vehicle, suddenly the rider applied the brake and vehicle has not been controlled by him, as a result of which, both the petitioner and rider fell down from the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and immediately he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Kadur for first aid treatment and then he was shifted to N.H. Hospital, Shimoga for better treatment,
wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
During the course of treatment, X-rays were taken and found the injuries all over the body and after discharge, doctor advised him to take bed rest and come for follow-up treatment

, thereby he had spent more than Rs.3 lakhs to hospitalization, medical expenses, conveyance, food,
nourishment and other incidental expenses.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and earning Rs.27,372/- p.m. as Police Constable and due to accidental injuries, he cannot able to do his work or any other work as before the accident.

Due to the accidental injuries, he suffered lot of pain and he has taken leave from his department, lost academic leave and sustained loss of happiness, physically and mentally, loss of amenities, loss of future prosperous, decreasing in life span and also sustained pain and agony.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 remained exparte and respondent No.2 appeared before the Tribunal and filed its Written Statement.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed in limine.
The alleged accident has been occurred on 10.08.2021 at about 7.30 p.m. by the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-EA-9620.
The statement made in column No.1 to 6, 8 to 14A of the claim petition are not admitted as not within the knowledge of this respondent.
The driver of the offending vehicle has not possessed the effective valid driving licence.
The insured/owner does not have proper and valid FC to use vehicle on the road.
The delay in lodging the complaint was not properly explained.

There was no compliance of mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) of MV Act either by insured or of section 158(6) of MV Act both by insured and concerned investigating police officer and insurer was kept in darkness in respect of alleged accident with ulterior motive to make insurer liable.
Further, the compensation amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the petition with costs.

Madhu.B vs Mallesha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40444872/
2 4.

From the above said pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he haD sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-18-EA-9620 on 10- 8-2021 at about 7.30 p.m. opposite Parvathamma farm, Doddabukkasagar road, Kadur Taluk,
Chikkamagaluru, Karnataka?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
5.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W1 and examined one witness PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P14 documents.
The respondent got examined one Dr.Gurumurthy H.R. as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1.

6. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 :
As per final order  for the following:-

REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1: In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-18-EA- 9620, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex-P1 to 14 i.e.,FIR, complaint, statement, crime details form, seizure mahazar, col.133 MV Act notice, reply to notice, IMV report, wound certificate,
charge sheet, discharge summary, adhar card, identity card, medical bills.

9. As per the petitioner, petitioner was going as pillion rider in the motor cycle bearing No.KA-18-EA -9620 on Doddabukkasagara road and while returning to his native place along with the rider Rudresh B.R. near Parvathamma farm, Kadur Taluk, at that time, the rider of the motor cycle drove the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden a cow came in front of the vehicle, suddenly the rider applied the brake and he was not able to control his vehicle and due to impact, both the petitioner and fell down and sustained injuries.
The respondent No.1 owner of the motor cycle remained exparte.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 insurance company filed Madhu.B vs Mallesha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40444872/
3 written statement.
On looking into the tenure of the cross examination made by the respondent No.2, respondent No.2 has not at all seriously disputed the cause and occurrence of the accident.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 suggested that PW-1 is stating false and the same has been outrightly denied by the PW-1.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 argued that there was a delay of one day in filing the complaint and petitioner has not properly explained the reason for the delay.

Further though petitioner stated that suddenly a cow came across the road, due to which rider of the motor cycle was not able to control the vehicle and fell down, but in the MLC, it is stated as skid and fall from the bike.

The respondent counsel examined Dr.Gurumurthy H.R. as RW-1 who in his evidence has clearly deposed that on 10-8-2021 at 7.30 p.m. petitioner came to him with the history of fall from the bike for treatment and thereafter he examined him and found unconscious and he has given first aid treatment and sent to the district hospital for higher treatment.
Further RW-1 produced MLC extract marked at Ex-R1.

On perusal of Ex-R1, it clearly shows that soon after the accident, petitioner was taken to the hospital and history of alleged injury is mentioned as skid and fall from bike, near Doddabukkasagara road.

Thus from the evidence of RW-1 and even Ex-R1,
it is clear that petitioner was a pillion rider along with rider on the motor cycle and petitioner had sustained injuries due to the fall from the bike.
It is not in dispute that the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 does not covers the risk of the pillion rider.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
10. There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Ex.P.8 IMV report indicates that the occurrence of the said accident was not due to any of the mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.

11. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
12. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

13. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not Madhu.B vs Mallesha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40444872/
4 required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
14. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-18-EA-9620.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
15. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 24 years.
The petitioner has produced aadhaar card and identity card as per Ex- P12 and 13, it reveals the year of birth of the petitioner was 1996.
So, as on the date of accident 10-8-2021
the petitioner was aged 25 years.
The petitioner has stated that he was working as Police constable and earning Rs.27,372/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.

16. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-
As per the Ex-P9-wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e., multiple parenchymal haemorrhage, B/L frontal lobes with diffuse axonal injury mild head injury and doctor opined that injuries are grievous in nature and Ex-P11-discharge summary of NH Sahyadri Narayana multispeciality hospital diagnosed multiple parenchymal haemorrhage, B/L frontal lobes with diffuse axonal injury mild head injury for which he took treatment as inpatient from 11-8-2021 to 28-8-2021 total period of 18 days.
17.
The petitioner has not examined doctor who treated him to assess the disability and discomfort suffered by him.
In the absence of any evidence on record with regard to disability, this tribunal not inclined to grant compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability.

18. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e.,multiple parenchymal haemorrhage, B/L frontal lobes with diffuse axonal injury mild head injury and doctor opined that injuries are grievous in nature and Ex-P11-discharge summary of NH Sahyadri Narayana multispeciality hospital diagnosed multiple parenchymal haemorrhage, B/L frontal lobes with diffuse axonal injury mild head injury for which petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 11-8-2021 to 28-8-2021 total period of 18 days.
The petitioner has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident.
The petitioner has stated that he is still suffering from disability and discomforts.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 25 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/- under this head.

Madhu.B vs Mallesha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40444872/
5 19.
LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:

By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the hospital for 18 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least two months.
But petitioner has not produced any document to show that he has suffered loss of pay for two months.
Hence petitioner is not entitle to loss of income during the laidup period.

20. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is residing in Kadur Taluk, Chikkamagaluru and has taken treatment at NH Sahyadri Narayana multispeciality hospital as inpatient from 11-8-2021 to 28- 8-2021 total period of 18 days and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital.

Admittedly, petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for 18 days and certainly,
it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of her treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.

Hence a sum of Rs.36,000/-
under this head.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The injuries referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of her life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the document as per Ex.P.14 i.e.,medical bills for Rs.1,13,503/-.
Even PW- 1 in his cross examination in para No.2 that he has claimed the medical bill from Arogya bhagya scheme and he got only some amount form the Arogya bhagya scheme.
But PW-1 has not clearly stated with regard to the extent of the bill which he got claimed from the Arogya bhagya scheme.
Even PW-1 has not produced any single document to prove the same.
Hence bill No.8 to 30 bills being the duplicate bills, thus court does not consider the said bill for granting compensation under the medical expenses.
23. PW-1 in his cross examination clearly admitted that bill No.8 to 30 bills are duplicate bills and also admitted that sl.No.2 and 3 bills amount has been mentioned in the bill No.4.
Hence bill No.8 to 30 and 4 being the duplicate bills cannot be taken into consideration.
Even the petitioner has not produced any document to show that he has taken the reimbursement.
Hence considering the Ex-P1 to 3 and bill No.6 and 7 bills i.e., for Rs.56,770/-.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.56,770/- under the head of medical expenses.

Madhu.B vs Mallesha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40444872/
6 24.

The calculation table stands as follows :
Pain and sufferings 75,000/-
Attendant charges, extra 35,000/-
nutritious food and conveyance charges Loss of future amenities and 25,000/-
happiness Medical expenses 56,770/-
Total 1,91,770/-
25.
INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
26. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
27. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,91,770/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, entire compensation amount shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
